description: Historical sections deleted at user request on 2026-09-30. These are archival regression inputs, never live answer requirements.

Q-2024F-FINAL-P09-a-ii.Common Mistakes:
- Here $B=2n^2+10000n+5n\log n$ has leading term $2n^2$; do not copy the preceding item's linear term. The ratio is $A/B\to5$. This finite positive limit gives both an upper and a lower bound; the large coefficient 10000 on a lower-order term does not change the classification.
- The official answer (ii) lists only $O$. That label is correct, but it omits the equally valid $\Omega$ and $\Theta$. Because all relations are requested, add both missing labels; do not claim that the official answer omitted $O$.

Q-2024F-FINAL-P09-a-iii.Common Mistakes:
- The entire exponent of five is $\log_2 n$, so rewrite it as $n^{\log_2 5}$. Since $\log_2 5>2$, the ratio is $n^{2-\log_2 5}\to0$, not a positive constant. Only $O$ holds: there is no positive lower bound for $\Omega$, and consequently no $\Theta$.
- The official answer (iii) writes $A=\Omega(B)$. This label is wrong: it incorrectly asserts that $n^2$ grows at least as fast as $B$; actually $n^2=o(B)$. Do not apply the previous item's finite-positive-limit case here. Keep the correct $O$ and exclude $\Omega$ and $\Theta$.

Q-2017-FINAL-P04-c.correction: Failed prime candidates are prime divisors of $T$, not of $n$. Also the printed strict inequality $\prod2>n$ is not justified by a set of $\log_2n$ factors. The valid bound is $2^r\le\prod_{i=1}^r\ell_i\le T<n$, whence at most $\lfloor\log_2T\rfloor+1=O(\log n)$ candidate tests.

Q-2020-FINAL1-P05-b.correction: The printed lower sum assumes an even integer $n$ and the strict upper inequality is not valid at the smallest cases. For all integer $n\ge4$, $\frac n4\log n\le\log(n!)\le n\log n$ supplies explicit bounds; finite small cases do not affect the asymptotic result.

Q-2016-FINAL-P06-a.correction: To justify that the displayed solution is the only one in the interval, put $q_1=7k$. Then $x=733+6930k$, and $0\le x<3000$ forces $k=0$. This supplies the interval check omitted after the source's candidate calculation.

Q-2018-FINAL-P12-b.correction: The printed $f(x)=2x,g(x)=x$ are not positive on the whole real domain. Take instead $g(x)=2^x,f(x)=2\cdot2^x$; their exponential ratio is $2^{2^x}\to\infty$, verifying the same conclusion with a fully valid counterexample.

checkpoints: transition from the sole base case $n=0$ to $n=1$
Q-2015-FINAL-P08-b.correction: The printed $n>1$ omits the transition from the sole base case $n=0$ to $n=1$. Use $n\ge1$ in the induction step; its displayed algebra then proves every required transition.

Q-2017-MID-P04-a.correction: The last printed comparison should be $1\not\equiv8\pmod2$, since $b+c=3+5=8$. In fact $1\equiv5\pmod2$. The proposed values do correctly refute the statement.

Q-2015-FINAL-P10.correction: The printed induction step covers only $2\le m\le n-1$, the range supplied by $p(n-1)$. For the new case $m=n$, directly use $n\mid n!=n(n-1)!$. Since $m\ge2$, the resulting residue one is the standard remainder. Including both cases completes the induction without changing its valid old-modulus argument.

Q-2018-FINAL-P04-a.correction: The intended basis is $1,2,3\in X$, equivalently $\{1,2,3\}\subseteq X$. The printed $\{1,2,3\}\in X$ instead describes a set-valued element and is not the intended integer basis.

Q-2015-MID-P02-c.correction: Printed line 5 cites lines (3,4). Modus ponens requires $p$, which is line 2, so the reference must be (2,4). The stated formula and conclusion are valid with that corrected citation.

Q-2017-MID-P01-c.correction: The printed condition that every $Q$ is false is insufficient alone. On the nonempty domain $\{a\}$ set $P(a)=T,Q(a)=F$; the antecedent is true and every inner implication is false. The non-tautology conclusion is correct.

Q-2018-FINAL-P05-b.correction: The printed answer omits $(m,n)=(1,1)$. This single-edge graph has exactly two odd-degree vertices and an open Euler trail, so it must be added.
